subject.title: feat: publish plugins with extended-stable releases

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this PR's all-plugin exact-core lockstep policy for every extended-stable `.33+` release, or should plugin publication wait for the monthly snapshot/covered-plugin policy in the overlapping open PRs?
rationale: The patch is technically coherent after the fallback fix, but it changes release policy and operator workflow contracts in an area with open competing implementation branches.

options.title: Adopt all-plugin lockstep here
options.body: Use this PR as the release path if maintainers want every npm-publishable official plugin to track the exact extended-stable core version for each `.33+` release.

options.title: Use the snapshot boundary
options.body: Pause or supersede this PR if maintainers prefer the monthly `.33` snapshot plus covered-plugin patch policy from the overlapping branch.

options.title: Keep core-only for now
options.body: Defer plugin publication and runtime convergence until a later release-design PR if the operational boundary is not ready.

recommendation.title: Adopt all-plugin lockstep here
recommendation.body: Use this PR as the release path if maintainers want every npm-publishable official plugin to track the exact extended-stable core version for each `.33+` release.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest current-main history signal for the release/plugin workflow surfaces and is the best available owner for the release-policy choice.
